purpose: Teach: ちがう/浮い/曲げ/騒い/脱い/滑り/冷やし/返せ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さん、本気で、絶対、ちがう、絶対、道、絶対、お選びになったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, remember when you were young? Your father—he took a completely different path in life. Do you remember that?
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Voice carries the weight of decades. Slight pause before 'different path' as if reaching back. Gentle insistence on the memory, not accusatory—just wanting to hold it together.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、池に、絶対、浮い、絶対、てる、絶対、お花、絶対、お好きだったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. And I remember when your grandfather was young—he absolutely loved floating flowers on the pond. You remember that about him, don't you?
lines.style: Warm, immediate reply. Her voice brightens slightly when she says 'floating flowers'—that detail still delights her. Affectionate lilt on 'dear.' Not correcting him, just adding her own thread.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、お背中、絶対、曲げ、絶対、ないで、絶対、お立ちだったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, your back was always so straight. Standing tall like that—do you remember?
lines.style: Voice quieter now, more intimate. A note of admiration underneath—not commenting on age, but on vitality. The question is tender, almost vulnerable. Trailing slightly as if he's seeing her across the years.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、お孫さんと、本気で、絶対、騒い、絶対、で、絶対、お遊びになったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: And your grandfather—when he was young, he'd run around and play so loudly with the grandchildren. You remember how wild he was, don't you?
lines.style: Bright, almost playful. Her voice lifts as she describes his energy. A small laugh underneath. The memory of his exuberance still touches her. Speaking to him fondly across time.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、上着、絶対、脱い、絶対、で、絶対、ご休憩、絶対、なさったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, you'd take your jacket off and rest like that. Do you remember those days?
lines.style: Voice slower, more measured. A gentle observation wrapped in the question. Not wistful exactly—matter-of-fact but lined with tenderness. The image of her resting, unburdened.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、雪道で、本気で、絶対、滑り、絶対、お転びになったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: And your grandfather—he slipped and fell on the snowy road once, badly. You remember how much that worried him, don't you?
lines.style: Soft concern layered underneath the memory. Not dramatic, just honest. A small shake in her voice—the worry was real, even now. Protective, the way she holds that memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、冷やし、絶対、たお茶、絶対、お父さんに、絶対、淹れてくれたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, you'd brew chilled tea on those hot days and bring it to me. Do you remember doing that?
lines.style: Voice warm and direct, almost marveling at the detail. The specific kindness of that gesture still moves him. Slight catch on 'chilled tea'—the care in it. Gratitude beneath remembering.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、お借りした本、本気で、絶対、返せ、絶対、ない、絶対、悔しがられたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: And I remember when your grandfather borrowed a book from me and couldn't bring himself to return it. He was so frustrated with himself about that. Do you remember?
lines.style: Gentle teasing mixed with understanding. A small, knowing laugh. She's not angry about the book—she's remembering his integrity, his embarrassment. The affection in how she holds even his failures.
